original_question: Compact Riemannian manifolds with negative curvature must be isometric if they have C^0 -conjugate geodesic flows.
target_in_paper: Conjecture 5.2.1 in §5.2 (The conjugacy problem). The paper first defines C^k-conjugate geodesic flows for two Riemannian manifolds and then states the conjecture that compact Riemannian manifolds with negative curvature must be isometric if they have C^0-conjugate geodesic flows. ([users.fmi.uni-jena.de](https://users.fmi.uni-jena.de/~matveev/Datei/problem_list_submitted.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact official target almost verbatim: it has the right class of objects (compact Riemannian manifolds), the right hypothesis (negative curvature plus C^0-conjugate geodesic flows), and the right conclusion (isometric). ([users.fmi.uni-jena.de](https://users.fmi.uni-jena.de/~matveev/Datei/problem_list_submitted.pdf))
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, the statement should name two manifolds, say (M1,g1) and (M2,g2), rather than speaking generically about manifolds. ([users.fmi.uni-jena.de](https://users.fmi.uni-jena.de/~matveev/Datei/problem_list_submitted.pdf))

The paper defines C^k-conjugate geodesic flows explicitly: there must be an invertible map h: SM1 -> SM2 such that h and h^{-1} are C^k and h o phi_1^t = phi_2^t o h for all t, where phi_i^t is the geodesic flow of g_i on the unit tangent bundle SM_i. For k=0 this means h is a homeomorphism. ([users.fmi.uni-jena.de](https://users.fmi.uni-jena.de/~matveev/Datei/problem_list_submitted.pdf))

If you want the hypothesis spelled out completely, the flows live on the unit tangent bundles SM1 and SM2, not directly on the manifolds themselves. ([users.fmi.uni-jena.de](https://users.fmi.uni-jena.de/~matveev/Datei/problem_list_submitted.pdf))

The conjecture is about negative curvature in the Riemannian sense used throughout §5, i.e. negatively curved metrics; writing this as negative sectional curvature makes the stand-alone formulation unambiguous. ([users.fmi.uni-jena.de](https://users.fmi.uni-jena.de/~matveev/Datei/problem_list_submitted.pdf))

The paper-faithful scope should not be broadened to the no-conjugate-points setting without extra assumptions: the authors explicitly warn that some restriction is needed and cite Zoll/Croke-Kleiner examples showing that the unrestricted extension would be false. ([users.fmi.uni-jena.de](https://users.fmi.uni-jena.de/~matveev/Datei/problem_list_submitted.pdf))
refined_question: Let (M1,g1) and (M2,g2) be compact Riemannian manifolds of negative sectional curvature, let phi_i^t denote the geodesic flow of g_i on the unit tangent bundle SM_i, and suppose there exists a homeomorphism h: SM1 -> SM2 such that h o phi_1^t = phi_2^t o h for every t in R. Must (M1,g1) and (M2,g2) be isometric? ([users.fmi.uni-jena.de](https://users.fmi.uni-jena.de/~matveev/Datei/problem_list_submitted.pdf))
justification: The draft is targeting the paper's official conjugacy conjecture, not a neighboring problem. Section 5.2 gives the needed nearby definition of C^k-conjugate geodesic flows and then states Conjecture 5.2.1 in essentially the same words as your draft. Section 5.1 supplies the motivation: Hamenstadt showed that, for negatively curved compact manifolds, equality of marked length spectrum forces C^0-conjugacy of geodesic flows, reducing that rigidity problem to this conjugacy conjecture. The same §5.2 passage also says one should not casually weaken negative curvature to no conjugate points without extra restrictions. ([users.fmi.uni-jena.de](https://users.fmi.uni-jena.de/~matveev/Datei/problem_list_submitted.pdf))
